techniques.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/semop.ts:26 The whole handed batch is one prompt string; there is no multi-level index to split keys across.

pairs.registryProposal: LOTUS sem_filter over a batch already in hand is a classifier, not this subject's semantic lane; the shared word semantic is not enough to apply the subject.

pairs.evidence: scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:68 The kNN probe orders by L2 distance and always keeps ten ids, with no distance cutoff, so a neighbourhood with nothing close still returns a full slice.

techniques.evidence: scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:49 The script always runs a fixed query count; there is no request that might not need the corpus.

scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:70 The first id is recorded as soon as the query returns; nothing rescores the ten.
scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:7 Ten is the latency metric's width on equal-sized ids, not a consumer budget split across lanes.
scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:68 Nearest-neighbour search with a fixed limit and no distance floor always returns k.

scripts/db-bench/vector.ts:101 The only correctness check is that two exact engines agree on top-1; it is not a labeled relevance set.

pairs.registryProposal: relevance-floors says every nearest-neighbour lane owes a floor, but its use_when is about returning nothing and about recalibrating after an embedder swap; it does not say whether an exact top-k latency probe, whose top-1 is only a cross-engine checksum, is in scope.
